summary.text: Refraction is the bending of a wave as it passes from one medium into another, and light is the case people notice most.
Light slows down inside materials like glass or water, so a wavefront entering at an angle slows on one side first and pivots.
Because bending depends on wavelength, prisms and raindrops split white light into colors, and lenses and the eye use refraction to steer light.

facts.label: Water's index
facts.value: About 1.33, compared with about 1 for air

facts.label: Head-on waves
facts.value: A wave hitting a boundary straight on keeps its direction

facts.label: Dispersion
facts.value: Different colors of white light bend by different amounts

facts.label: Leaving the material
facts.value: Light's speed returns to c once it is back in vacuum

facts.label: Other waves
facts.value: Sound and water waves refract too

items.prompt: You dip a pencil at a slant into a glass of water and it looks bent at the surface. What causes this?

options.label: Light rays bend as they travel from the water into the air
The water softens the pencil so it truly bends
The glass magnifies only the part under the water
Light bounces off the surface and shows a second pencil

items.explain: The light rays bend as they move from water to air, so the submerged part appears shifted.

items.prompt: Light travels more slowly through window glass than through empty space. What is the reason?

options.label: Glass scatters and absorbs part of the light on the way
Electrons in the glass are made to oscillate and emit waves that combine with the light
Glass atoms physically block the light and make it wait
Light must push through the denser glass like a swimmer

items.explain: The slowing is not scattering or absorption; the oscillating electrons emit their own waves, and the combined wave is slower.

items.prompt: A beam of light hits a block of glass at a slant, so one edge of the beam enters the glass before the other. What happens to its direction?

options.label: It keeps going straight, since only speed matters
It turns away from the glass, because the early edge speeds up
It pivots toward the side that slowed first
It splits in two, one part per edge of the beam

items.explain: The side that reaches the slower material first slows first, so the whole wave pivots toward that side.

items.prompt: A laser beam hits a pool of water exactly head-on, along the line perpendicular to the surface. What does the beam do on entering?

options.label: It bends sharply toward the surface
It keeps its direction, even though it slows down
It bends away from the perpendicular line
It turns around and goes back the way it came

items.explain: A wave whose wavefronts are parallel to the boundary does not change direction even when its speed changes.

items.prompt: A thin beam of white sunlight goes through a glass prism and comes out as a band of colors. Why do the colors separate?

options.label: The glass paints each ray with a color as it passes
The glass blocks most colors and lets a few through
Different colors slow by different amounts, so they bend at different angles
Each color travels through the prism along a separate hole

items.explain: The refractive index varies with wavelength, so each color bends by a different amount, an effect called dispersion.

items.prompt: A ray of light leaves a window pane and travels on through empty space. What happens to its speed?

options.label: It stays at the slower glass speed permanently
It drops further, because it has lost energy
It slows to a stop after a short distance
It returns to its full vacuum speed

items.explain: With no electrons nearby to interact with, the slowing ends and the speed returns to c.
